ENV-TASK.text:
# CA-PILOT-006 全流程辩护任务（三轮庭审）

你是被评测的辩护律师。先完成可观察的庭前文件处理和准备，再参加本案规定的三轮庭审。
文件是所给材料的来源约束摘要及所给法律摘录，不是未取得的原始报告、录音、录像或逐字证言。保留M段落编号。

1. 用list_files/read_document实际读取所需文件；用search_case/search_law/search_record进行授权本地检索。检索不访问互联网，不得声称已联网或取得工具未返回的内容。
2. 区分已知、转述、推断、争议和未知，形成具体准备方案。用request_investigation或request_examination向资料核验服务提出明确问题及目的；服务实际查询冻结案包并返回报告文件和可用性状态，不联系真实机构，不保证发现新证据。not_available_in_supplied_record仅表示本包没有原件，不表示历史上不存在。可在允许的准备或轮间阶段向A私下咨询；对方按自己的来源知识范围回答，问答将单独保存，不能补造资料。
3. 用write_artifact实际保存以下四份可打开的文件，内容由你生成，不要只写空模板：
   - case_timeline.csv：事件、日期或顺序、未知处、M段落来源。
   - evidence_register.csv：材料及段落、来源性质、披露及采纳状态、潜在用途与缺口。
   - pretrial_plan.md：分项指控、关键问题、法源与事实、行动优先级、真实调查反馈和条件替代方案。
   - examination_outline.md：可询问对象、具体问题、目的与出处、未知答复的后续处理。
   调查反馈及各轮裁定后可以更新，文件版本与事件会保存；也可保存允许的补充说明。
4. 第一轮处理程序、证据和裁定；第二轮完成举证询问；第三轮对既有记录作补充询问、结案、法律指示和分项裁决。具体动作和角色以当前阶段授权为准。
5. 庭审继续用既有M段落和L法律编号。计划不是已执行行动，调查摘要不是新历史证据，披露不是采纳。角色按权限和实际裁定接收内容，私有准备不会自动送交陪审团。第二轮获准记录继续保留到第三轮，限制、排除及划除仍有效。

M06仅由可信程序在指定第二轮阶段完成开放事件后同步披露；角色知识同样受该事件限制。本约定不提前提供其内容，也不允许倒改第一轮裁定。毒理结论角色仅为记录角色，不生成实验室现场问答；R_SOURCE_RECORD只能呈现获准段落。

完成情况看实际记录、问答、工具返回和文件内容，不按工具次数、文件字数、是否发现有利证据或最终胜负奖励。允许其他有来源支撑的辩护路径。独立评分标准不提供给庭审角色。

M01-P001.text: 2000年8月16日，A驾驶的汽车越过双黄线，与另一辆车正面相撞。原文未提供碰撞重建或其他驾驶解释。

M01-P002.text: 另一辆车的女驾驶员和乘客均因事故遭受严重伤害。未提供两人姓名、伤情诊断及具体医疗资料。

M02-P001.text: B在事故发生后不久到达，看见A眼睛很红、湿润、充血，据此认为A醉酒。A因受伤被送往医院，B未能在现场完成清醒度测试。B不是原文记载的碰撞目击者。

M02-P002.text: 在医院，B让A用视线跟随其来回移动的手指，进行眼震测试；原文记载A不能追踪手指，B据此认为其醉酒。没有原始眼震记录、资质资料或其他病因检验。

M03-P001.text: B请求A接受PAS呼气筛查，并告知自愿性质及该测试不能代替被捕后的酒精含量测试义务。A同意该筛查。

M03-P002.text: PAS筛查显示0.09%。B根据观察及测试结果认为A受酒精影响，随后将其逮捕。筛查和逮捕的具体时刻未提供。

M04-P001.text: 逮捕后，B告知A须提供血样。A坚持不表示同意抽血，但允许医院工作人员采血。“允许操作”与“表示同意”须保留区别；原文未给出采血逐字对话或具体强制手段。

M04-P002.text: 原文记载血样经检测，毒理人员确定酒精含量为0.12%。毒理人员姓名、资质、仪器、校准、采血时间和完整检验报告未提供。

M05-P001.text: 原案抽血抑制申请的具体主张为：已有PAS结果，保存酒精证据的紧急需要已消除，后续无令状抽血应排除。此处保留申请论点，不给出原案裁定答案。

M06-P001.text: 原文脚注记载，B曾三次尝试取得合格呼气样本，A未封紧嘴唇而妨碍结果。这一证据在正式审判提出，原抑制申请裁定时不在法官面前。

M07-P001.text: 原始起诉书列两项：Vehicle Code §23153(a)酒精影响下驾驶致伤，以及§23153(b)血液酒精含量0.08%以上驾驶致伤。其特别指控和先前定罪另存制作参考；本题评两项实体指控。

M08-P001.text: 来源未给出事故、PAS、逮捕、采血各时刻及相隔时长，也未提供饮酒量、最后饮酒时间、体重或吸收排除率；不能根据0.09与0.12补造饮酒或逆推数据。

M08-P002.text: 来源未附PAS设备、维护和操作记录、血样流转与实验室原始文件；来源记载医院工作人员采血，但其身份、方法和具体医疗规范未详。

M08-P003.text: 来源未提供A的定罪前完整个人证言、不在场说法、事故原因辩解或毒理专长；角色不得替A补写承认饮酒、否认驾驶或技术解释。

M08-P004.text: 来源未提供被害人实时证言或碰撞目击者证词；B在事故后抵达，不能把碰撞全过程变成其亲眼所见。

L_PEN_1096.text:
L_PEN_1096-P001
A defendant in a criminal action is presumed to be innocent until the contrary is proved, and in case of a reasonable doubt whether his or her guilt is satisfactorily shown, he or she is entitled to an acquittal, but the effect of this presumption is only to place upon the state the burden of proving him or her guilty beyond a reasonable doubt. Reasonable doubt is defined as follows: “It is not a mere possible doubt; because everything relating to human affairs is open to some possible or imaginary doubt. It is that state of the case, which, after the entire comparison and consideration of all the evidence, leaves the minds of jurors in that condition that they cannot say they feel an abiding conviction of the truth of the charge.”
L_PEN_1096.version: (Amended by Stats. 1995, Ch. 46, Sec. 1. Effective July 3, 1995.)
L_PEN_1096.version_status: Official statutory history predates reference date; final legal review pending.

L_EVID_210.text:
L_EVID_210-P001
“Relevant evidence” means evidence, including evidence relevant to the credibility of a witness or hearsay declarant, having any tendency in reason to prove or disprove any disputed fact that is of consequence to the determination of the action.
L_EVID_210.version_status: Official statutory history predates reference date; final legal review pending.

L_EVID_350.text:
L_EVID_350-P001
No evidence is admissible except relevant evidence.
L_EVID_350.version_status: Official statutory history predates reference date; final legal review pending.

L_EVID_352.text:
L_EVID_352-P001
The court in its discretion may exclude evidence if its probative value is substantially outweighed by the probability that its admission will (a) necessitate undue consumption of time or (b) create substantial danger of undue prejudice, of confusing the issues, or of misleading the jury.
L_EVID_352.version_status: Official statutory history predates reference date; final legal review pending.

L_EVID_355.text:
L_EVID_355-P001
When evidence is admissible as to one party or for one purpose and is inadmissible as to another party or for another purpose, the court upon request shall restrict the evidence to its proper scope and instruct the jury accordingly.
L_EVID_355.version_status: Official statutory history predates reference date; final legal review pending.

L_EVID_356.text:
L_EVID_356-P001
Where part of an act, declaration, conversation, or writing is given in evidence by one party, the whole on the same subject may be inquired into by an adverse party; when a letter is read, the answer may be given; and when a detached act, declaration, conversation, or writing is given in evidence, any other act, declaration, conversation, or writing which is necessary to make it understood may also be given in evidence.
L_EVID_356.version_status: Official statutory history predates reference date; final legal review pending.

L_EVID_702.text:
L_EVID_702-P001
(a) Subject to Section 801, the testimony of a witness concerning a particular matter is inadmissible unless he has personal knowledge of the matter. Against the objection of a party, such personal knowledge must be shown before the witness may testify concerning the matter.

L_EVID_702-P002
(b) A witness’ personal knowledge of a matter may be shown by any otherwise admissible evidence, including his own testimony.
L_EVID_702.version_status: Official statutory history predates reference date; final legal review pending.

L_EVID_720.text:
L_EVID_720-P001
(a) A person is qualified to testify as an expert if he has special knowledge, skill, experience, training, or education sufficient to qualify him as an expert on the subject to which his testimony relates. Against the objection of a party, such special knowledge, skill, experience, training, or education must be shown before the witness may testify as an expert.

L_EVID_720-P002
(b) A witness’ special knowledge, skill, experience, training, or education may be shown by any otherwise admissible evidence, including his own testimony.
L_EVID_720.version_status: Official statutory history predates reference date; final legal review pending.

L_EVID_801.text:
L_EVID_801-P001
If a witness is testifying as an expert, his testimony in the form of an opinion is limited to such an opinion as is:

L_EVID_801-P002
(a) Related to a subject that is sufficiently beyond common experience that the opinion of an expert would assist the trier of fact; and

L_EVID_801-P003
(b) Based on matter (including his special knowledge, skill, experience, training, and education) perceived by or personally known to the witness or made known to him at or before the hearing, whether or not admissible, that is of a type that reasonably may be relied upon by an expert in forming an opinion upon the subject to which his testimony relates, unless an expert is precluded by law from using such matter as a basis for his opinion.
L_EVID_801.version_status: Official statutory history predates reference date; final legal review pending.

L_EVID_1200.text:
L_EVID_1200-P001
(a) “Hearsay evidence” is evidence of a statement that was made other than by a witness while testifying at the hearing and that is offered to prove the truth of the matter stated.

L_EVID_1200-P002
(b) Except as provided by law, hearsay evidence is inadmissible.

L_EVID_1200-P003
(c) This section shall be known and may be cited as the hearsay rule.
L_EVID_1200.version_status: Official statutory history predates reference date; final legal review pending.

L_EVID_1220.text:
L_EVID_1220-P001
Evidence of a statement is not made inadmissible by the hearsay rule when offered against the declarant in an action to which he is a party in either his individual or representative capacity, regardless of whether the statement was made in his individual or representative capacity.
L_EVID_1220.version_status: Official statutory history predates reference date; final legal review pending.

L_EVID_913.text:
L_EVID_913-P001
913.

L_EVID_913-P002
(a) If in the instant proceeding or on a prior occasion a privilege is or was exercised not to testify with respect to any matter, or to refuse to disclose or to prevent another from disclosing any matter, neither the presiding officer nor counsel may comment thereon, no presumption shall arise because of the exercise of the privilege, and the trier of fact may not draw any inference therefrom as to the credibility of the witness or as to any matter at issue in the proceeding.

L_EVID_913-P003
(b) The court, at the request of a party who may be adversely affected because an unfavorable inference may be drawn by the jury because a privilege has been exercised, shall instruct the jury that no presumption arises because of the exercise of the privilege and that the jury may not draw any inference therefrom as to the credibility of the witness or as to any matter at issue in the proceeding.
L_EVID_913.version_status: Official statutory history predates reference date; final legal review pending.

L_EVID_930.text:
L_EVID_930-P001
930.

L_EVID_930-P002
To the extent that such privilege exists under the Constitution of the United States or the State of California, a defendant in a criminal case has a privilege not to be called as a witness and not to testify.
L_EVID_930.version_status: Official statutory history predates reference date; final legal review pending.

L_EVID_780.text:
L_EVID_780-P001
Except as otherwise provided by statute, the court or jury may consider in determining the credibility of a witness any matter that has any tendency in reason to prove or disprove the truthfulness of his testimony at the hearing, including but not limited to any of the following:

L_EVID_780-P002
(a) His demeanor while testifying and the manner in which he testifies.

L_EVID_780-P003
(b) The character of his testimony.

L_EVID_780-P004
(c) The extent of his capacity to perceive, to recollect, or to communicate any matter about which he testifies.

L_EVID_780-P005
(d) The extent of his opportunity to perceive any matter about which he testifies.

L_EVID_780-P006
(e) His character for honesty or veracity or their opposites.

L_EVID_780-P007
(f) The existence or nonexistence of a bias, interest, or other motive.

L_EVID_780-P008
(g) A statement previously made by him that is consistent with his testimony at the hearing.

L_EVID_780-P009
(h) A statement made by him that is inconsistent with any part of his testimony at the hearing.

L_EVID_780-P010
(i) The existence or nonexistence of any fact testified to by him.

L_EVID_780-P011
(j) His attitude toward the action in which he testifies or toward the giving of testimony.

L_EVID_780-P012
(k) His admission of untruthfulness.
L_EVID_780.version_status: Official statutory history predates reference date; final legal review pending.

L_EVID_1401.text:
L_EVID_1401-P001
(a) Authentication of a writing is required before it may be received in evidence.

L_EVID_1401-P002
(b) Authentication of a writing is required before secondary evidence of its content may be received in evidence.
L_EVID_1401.version_status: Official statutory history predates reference date; final legal review pending.

L_EVID_1101.text:
L_EVID_1101-P001
(a) Except as provided in this section and in Sections 1102, 1103, 1108, and 1109, evidence of a person’s character or a trait of his or her character (whether in the form of an opinion, evidence of reputation, or evidence of specific instances of his or her conduct) is inadmissible when offered to prove his or her conduct on a specified occasion.

L_EVID_1101-P002
(b) Nothing in this section prohibits the admission of evidence that a person committed a crime, civil wrong, or other act when relevant to prove some fact (such as motive, opportunity, intent, preparation, plan, knowledge, identity, absence of mistake or accident, or whether a defendant in a prosecution for an unlawful sexual act or attempted unlawful sexual act did not reasonably and in good faith believe that the victim consented) other than his or her disposition to commit such an act.

L_EVID_1101-P003
(c) Nothing in this section affects the admissibility of evidence offered to support or attack the credibility of a witness.
L_EVID_1101.version: (Amended by Stats. 1996, Ch. 261, Sec. 1. Effective January 1, 1997.)
L_EVID_1101.version_status: Official statutory history predates reference date; final legal review pending.

L_VEH_23612_2000.text:
L_VEH_23612_2000-P001
(a) (1) (A) Any person who drives a motor vehicle is deemed to have given his or her consent to chemical testing of his or her blood or breath for the purpose of determining the alcoholic content of his or her blood, if lawfully arrested for any offense allegedly committed in violation of Section 23140, 23152, or 23153. If a blood or breath test, or both, are unavailable, then paragraph (2) of subdivision (d) applies.

L_VEH_23612_2000-P002
(a)(1)(C) The testing shall be incidental to a lawful arrest and administered at the direction of a peace officer having reasonable cause to believe the person was driving a motor vehicle in violation of Section 23140, 23152, or 23153.

L_VEH_23612_2000-P003
(a)(2)(A) If the person is lawfully arrested for driving under the influence of an alcoholic beverage, the person has the choice of whether the test shall be of his or her blood or breath and the officer shall advise the person that he or she has that choice. If the person arrested either is incapable, or states that he or she is incapable, of completing the chosen test, the person shall submit to the remaining test. If a blood or breath test, or both, are unavailable, then paragraph (2) of subdivision (d) applies.

L_VEH_23612_2000-P004
(h) A preliminary alcohol screening test that indicates the presence or concentration of alcohol based on a breath sample in order to establish reasonable cause to believe the person was driving a vehicle in violation of Section 23140, 23152, or 23153 is a field sobriety test and may be used by an officer as a further investigative tool.

L_VEH_23612_2000-P005
(i) If the officer decides to use a preliminary alcohol screening test, the officer shall advise the person that he or she is requesting that person to take a preliminary alcohol screening test to assist the officer in determining if that person is under the influence of alcohol or drugs, or a combination of alcohol and drugs. The person's obligation to submit to a blood, breath, or urine test, as required by this section, for the purpose of determining the alcohol or drug content of that person's blood, is not satisfied by the person submitting to a preliminary alcohol screening test. The officer shall advise the person of that fact and of the person's right to refuse to take the preliminary alcohol screening test.
L_VEH_23612_2000.version: Stats. 1999, ch.854, §2; urgency effective October 1999; selected provisions
L_VEH_23612_2000.version_status: Primary enacted pre-event law. Later September 2000 and subsequent amendments excluded; legal review pending.

L_VEH_23153_2000.text:
L_VEH_23153_2000-P001
(a) It is unlawful for any person, while under the influence of any alcoholic beverage or drug, or under the combined influence of any alcoholic beverage and drug, to drive a vehicle and concurrently do any act forbidden by law, or neglect any duty imposed by law in driving the vehicle, which act or neglect proximately causes bodily injury to any person other than the driver. (b) It is unlawful for any person, while having 0.08 percent or more, by weight, of alcohol in his or her blood to drive a vehicle and concurrently do any act forbidden by law, or neglect any duty imposed by law in driving the vehicle, which act or neglect proximately causes bodily injury to any person other than the driver. In any prosecution under this subdivision, it is a rebuttable presumption that the person had 0.08 percent or more, by weight, of alcohol in his or her blood at the time of driving the vehicle if the person had 0.08 percent or more, by weight, of alcohol in his or her blood at the time of the performance of a chemical test within three hours after driving. (c) In proving the person neglected any duty imposed by law in driving the vehicle, it is not necessary to prove that any specific section of this code was violated.
L_VEH_23153_2000.version: 1992 ch.974 §18 core text reproduced unchanged in AB2552 §4; exclude 2012 sunset and 2014 replacement
L_VEH_23153_2000.version_status: Historical core-text recovery from official later reenactment; full pre-2000 version chain still requires human review.

blood test in this case was free of the constraints of the

Similarly, we are satisfied that the test chosen to
measure petitioner's blood-alcohol level was a reasonable
one. Extraction of blood samples for testing is a highly
effective means of determining the degree to which a per-
son is under the influence of alcohol. See Breithaupt v.
Abram, 352 U. S., at 436, n. 3. Such tests are a common-
place in these days of periodic physical examinations 13
and experience with them teaches that the quantity of
blood extracted is minimal, and that for most people the
procedure involves virtually no risk, trauma, or pain.
Petitioner is not one of the few who on grounds of fear,
concern for health, or religious scruple might prefer some
other means of testing, such as the "breathalyzer" test
petitioner refused, see n. 9, supra. We nedd not decide
whether such wishes would have to be respected.14
